claims.text: At stage-3 POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/refund answers 202 Accepted with the order in status refunding; the order's change and its order.refund-requested outbox row are saved in one transaction.
Payments' background job keeps retrying a failing gateway for up to 24 hours from requested_at, so the refund can stay unfinished far longer than seconds.
At stage-2 Order.Ship() accepted an order in status paid and Order.Cancel() accepted new or paid; at stage-2 a paid order could be cancelled.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs (Ship, Cancel); stage-3 OrderTests.cs:63-65 comment

claims.text: At PostgreSQL's default isolation level (Read Committed), other transactions do not see a transaction's changes until it commits.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, 13.2.1 Read Committed Isolation Level

claims.text: Order.RequestRefund() throws refund-in-progress for a refunding order, not-paid for any other non-paid status, and otherwise sets refunding and records OrderRefundRequested.
Order.Ship() and Order.Cancel() throw OrderStatusException with code refund-in-progress for a refunding order; Cancel() throws code paid for a paid order. Each check throws before Status is assigned.
ExceptionHandlingMiddleware turns OrderStatusException into 409 Conflict Problem Details whose type is a base address followed by the exception's code (e.g. ending in refund-in-progress).
Order.CompleteRefund() accepts only a refunding order (code not-refunding otherwise) and sets it to cancelled; DonHang.Api calls it when payment.refunded arrives.
The stage-2 version of refund-design.md left open whether a paid order may still be cancelled; the stage-3 version records it as closed: Order.Cancel() refuses paid orders.

OrderTests at stage-3 has Cancel_PaidOrder_Throws (code paid, status stays paid) and RequestRefund_RefundingOrder_Throws, Cancel_RefundingOrder_Throws, Ship_RefundingOrder_Throws; none uses a database, RabbitMQ or Payments.

refund-design.md step 2: while the order is refunding, a second refund request, cancelling and shipping are refused with 409 (YC-4). YC-4 itself: the customer cannot send a second request for the same order.
A PostgreSQL row lock is held until the end of the transaction that took it; another transaction that tries to update or lock that row waits until the holder commits or rolls back.
The code that publishes outbox rows to RabbitMQ (OutboxRelay) reads outbox_messages in its own transactions, so it cannot see an outbox row until the transaction that wrote it commits.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Messaging/OutboxRelay.cs; PostgreSQL 17 docs 13.2.1 Read Committed

claims.text: With Entities.cs line 126 commented out, Cancel() on a refunding order passes the cancelled/shipped/paid checks, sets cancelled, and Cancel_RefundingOrder_Throws fails; CompleteRefund() would then refuse that order (not-refunding).
Opinion: when a saga leaves an entity unfinished between steps, mark it with a status that the entity's own methods check, rather than holding a lock across the saga or leaving the check to a client.
